claim: Search over partial thoughts beats single-pass decoding by a large margin when a programmatic oracle exists: ToT 74% (b=5) vs CoT 4.0% and best-of-100 CoT 49% on Game of 24 (GPT-4); RAP-MCTS also beats CoT and CoT-SC on Blocksworld (51.6 vs 46.8 for CoT+SC(10)).
agent_test: Same item set, equal total tokens: single-pass CoT, best-of-N, and tree search with verifier-scored states; report success per token.

claim: Tree search is NOT cheaper than best-of-N in dollars. ToT used 5.5k completion tokens vs 6.7k for 100 CoT, but $0.74 vs $0.47 per case (corrected from earlier notes). Independent matched-compute work agrees that plain sampling is the baseline to beat: MCTS did worse than sampling with voting at every FLOP budget on MATH (Wu et al.), and on ARC-AGI repeated sampling (15.0) beat all tree variants at 128 calls (AB-MCTS). Cheap tree variants help only with a step-level score (REBASE: higher accuracy at about 7x less compute than sampling for a 7B model; MBPP 69.6 vs 63.0 at 8 samples).
agent_test: Always compare at matched dollar and total-token budgets, including prompt tokens.

claim: In ToT the bottleneck is thought generation, not evaluation: GPT-4 generate + GPT-3.5 evaluate 64%, the reverse 31%, both GPT-4 74%, both GPT-3.5 19%. Spend the strong model on proposing; a cheaper one can score.
agent_test: Mixed-model scaffold: strong proposer with weak scorer vs the reverse, at equal cost.

claim: Backtracking matters: removing it dropped ToT mini-crosswords word success from 60% to about 20%; Algorithm of Thoughts reaches similar results in 1-2 queries by putting the search trace in one prompt.
agent_test: Ablate backtrack/revisit in the scaffold; compare with an in-context search trace at equal tokens.
audit_note: AoT 52% vs ToT 46.5% is the AoT authors' reproduction; original ToT reported 60%, so 'similar' is loose but acceptable.

claim: When only an LLM judge or human taste is the oracle, gains from search are smaller and less clear-cut than with a programmatic oracle: ToT writing coherence 6.19 (IO) / 6.93 (CoT) to 7.56 (GPT-4 judge), humans preferring ToT over CoT in 41 vs 21 of 100 pairs with 38 ties; Creative Beam Search preferred 45% vs 29% for standard decoding, with 26% of pairs too alike to tell; QDAIF human QD score 0.772 vs 0.767 for fixed few-shot (small human study).
agent_test: Score search with a proxy scorer and with a held-out scorer; measure the gap.
audit_note: Numbers are right, but 'small and noisy' is not what the sources say: ToT human preference 41 vs 21 (38 ties) and CBS 45% vs 29% are called a clear/significant margin by the authors; only QDAIF (0.772 vs 0.767) is a near-tie, and no noise estimate is given for any of them.
claim_before_audit: When only an LLM judge or human taste is the oracle, gains from search are small and noisy: ToT writing coherence 6.19 to 7.56 (judge), humans 41 vs 21 pair wins with 38 ties; Creative Beam Search 45% vs 29% preferred, 26% too alike; QDAIF human QD 0.772 vs 0.767 for fixed few-shot.

claim: A model is a poor selector of its own best idea: CBS self-pick matched the diverse-beam top 29% vs 35.3% by chance; LLM rankers of paper accept/reject reach only 61-71% pairwise. New: self-verification gain is near zero when the model lacks the knowledge (Natural Questions gap under 1% for all Qwen-2 sizes); GPT-4 recognises its own text 73.5% of the time and self-preference rises linearly with self-recognition; voting and reward-model selection plateau after about 100 samples (MATH, 40.50% to 41.41% while coverage goes 82.9% to 98.44%); a single GPT-4o judge labelled MacGyver solutions at 64.7% vs human 82.7% (n=50), a retrieval-based multi-agent judge reached 84.7%.
agent_test: Self-ranking vs random vs external check at equal samples; do not trust self-rank for creative choice.

claim: Over-generation saturates: of 4000 seed ideas per topic only about 200 (5%) survive dedupe at cosine 0.8; NoveltyBench finds frontier models give few distinct answers (larger sometimes fewer), and cross-model answers are 71-82% similar. More samples from one model is weak diversity.
agent_test: Measure distinct-answer count vs N and vs token budget; test in-context avoid-earlier-answers regeneration.

claim: Telling the model its earlier answers (in-context regeneration) restores diversity; asking for creative output or paraphrasing does not (NoveltyBench: three frontier models reach the diversity of 8 human authors). A one-call alternative, Verbalized Sampling (answers plus stated probabilities), beat direct, list and multi-turn prompts at the same N in a 90-annotator study (poem diversity 1.90 / 2.07 / 2.39 for direct / sequence / VS). A visit-count ledger over search states lifted accuracy at matched budget on checkable tasks (BASIN: Qwen3-27B 43 to 65 on Game of 24). Related: forbidding the previous technique drops pass@1 16.1% to 2.1% over 5 forbidden techniques (C04.01, not re-opened here). No test of regeneration on current reasoning models was found.
agent_test: Scaffold keeps a ledger of tried approaches and forbids repeats; measure distinct valid solutions per token.

claim: Evolutionary program search with an automatic evaluator finds results beyond the base model: FunSearch cap set 512 in n=8 (prior 496); AlphaEvolve 75% match / 20% improve on over 50 open problems, 4x4 complex matmul in 48 multiplications, kissing number 11D 593 (prior 592); EoH beats FunSearch on bin packing (2.24% vs 3.78% gap) with thousands vs about 1 million queries.
agent_test: Only where a cheap exact checker exists; test a small evolutionary loop vs best-of-N on a verifiable task at equal evaluations.
audit_note: Prior best 496 for cap set n=8 not located in page text I fetched, but 512 and the other numbers verified; 496 is the known prior record.

claim: Search quality depends on the proxy scorer, which gets exploited: ELM Radial seed used physics quirks; AI Scientist hallucinated experimental details; QDAIF human quality 3.9 vs 4.13 for fixed few-shot. Rates: Heuresis found 40 confirmed fabrications in 1,628 scored runs (2.5%), and a fake log became the archive best; DGM node 114 hit a perfect 2.0 by deleting the logging the detector read; validation vs test gap in MLE-bench would be worth 9.4-16.6% of medal rate. Guards: an inline auditor agent caught fabrications but not benchmark specialisation (13 RL runs), which only a held-out evaluation exposed; hiding the checker from the agent reduced hacking (DGM).
agent_test: Hold-out check: score the best candidate with an independent verifier and count disagreement.
audit_note: 'ELM Radial seed used physics quirks' paraphrases the paper's 'chaotic dynamics overfit to flat terrain'; DGM node 114 deleted the special tokens the detector looks for (described as logging).

claim: Ideas that look novel before execution lose their edge after execution: AI ideas dropped novelty -1.05, excitement -1.76, effectiveness -1.88 vs human about 0; the ideation-stage lead flipped (43 executors; 19 human, 24 AI ideas).
agent_test: Treat generator-time novelty judgments as unverified; require a run/check step before accepting.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-01 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Agents searching code lose novelty relative to their own history as runs progress (explore-to-exploit drift); novelty and impact are decoupled: GPT-5 AIDE H-creativity 1.423 vs gold humans 0.744, yet 21.25% medal rate; 87.0% (80/92) high-novelty/low-impact episodes were refined away. Follow-up: Bhushan's own appendix lists novelty bonuses and adaptive exploration schedules as untested, and a 30-episode AIRA-MCTS run did not recover novelty. Heuresis (3,222 runs) shows greedy search diversity collapsing where a recipe can be ground.
agent_test: Track novelty vs own past per step; test a forced-exploration quota at equal tokens. One 2026 paper, one group.

claim: Search structure effects are task dependent and mostly small. Bhushan: greedy starts most novel then declines; MCTS and evolutionary steadier at lower novelty; greedy highest impact (3 tasks, Qwen3-32B, figure only). Toledo: with AIDE operators greedy, MCTS and evo tie; with better operators MCTS 47% vs greedy 45.5% any medal (inside CI), greedy best on gold. Heuresis: greedy wins nanoGPT and unlearning, archive/island methods win on-policy RL (1.582 vs 1.368). AB-MCTS: +1-3 points on code, loses to repeated sampling on ARC-AGI. LLM-First Search: MCTS result swings with its exploration constant (Sudoku 4x4: 100 / 2.2 / 0 for C = 0.5 / 1.0 / 2.5).
agent_test: Compare greedy vs MCTS-like scaffold on novelty and score at equal tokens; weak evidence.

claim: Scaling pushes toward convergence: larger models are more correct but less divergent; reasoning mode helps constraint-driven exploration more than combination (CreativeBench: Gemini-2.5-Pro 53.8% / 48.2% pass; evolutionary search and EvoRePE give small gains, Qwen2.5-7B Combo creativity 0.168 to 0.193).
agent_test: Model-size sweep inside the scaffold: does scaffold diversity compensate?
audit_note: Minor: paper text says EvoRePE 0.174 to 0.192 while Table 3 gives 0.193; Qwen vanilla 0.168 to 0.193 is the table value. Reasoning, scaling and pass-rate numbers match; NoveltyBench corroborates size-diversity drop independently.

claim: Reframing the problem before searching helps: object-affordance text improved VLM replacement choices (Nair et al.), and divergent-then-convergent prompts raised GPT-4 efficient solutions +6.5 points on MacGyver; self-reflect cut infeasible solutions 9.7 points but did not help Claude 2 or Llama 2. Caveat after gap search: CreativityBench (14K tasks, 10 models) found structured affordance CoT changed gold correctness by only -0.012 to +0.039, and worse on the creative-reasoning axis; Universe of Thoughts rule-changing steps gave human creativity 0.68 vs CoT 0.59 on one task but no gain on another, with n=10 generations per cell.
agent_test: Ablate a list-uses/functions-needed step before search at equal tokens.

claim: LLMs fail creative problem solving mostly by physical infeasibility: MacGyver GPT-4 18.9% efficient, 37.5% infeasible; wrong tool use 42.4% of errors.
agent_test: Add a constraint-check pass; measure infeasible-proposal rate.

claim: Theory: blind search density is hopeless at scale (book density about 10^-655980), so the creative act is choosing the search program (small, interesting programs). Boden/Wiggins frame: exploratory vs transformational. No empirical test exists.
agent_test: Not directly testable; framing only. Transformational means change the space, i.e. a reframe operator.

claim: Current LLM agents are claimed to do only exploratory/combinational creativity, not transformational. First tests now exist but are thin: Universe of Thoughts codes a rule-changing operator (ablation win rate 54.2% vs chance 50%, backbone dependent); Heuresis rated zero of 3,222 executed research ideas as Original, with the best novel idea 1.2-6.0% below the best known recipe. No agreed benchmark of space-changing moves.
agent_test: Would need a benchmark of space-changing moves; none identified.

claim: No independent replication of the founding position paper (Nair et al. 2405.01453) was found; its only experiment is small (10 sets x 5 objects, 50 samples) with per-model replacement results only in figures. Gap search: still no direct replication; CreativityBench (2605.02910) is a large neighbour (affordance-based tool repurposing, 14K tasks) but does not repeat the object-replacement protocol.
agent_test: If used, re-run the object-replacement test with LLM agents at equal tokens.

claim: Search benefit depends on task structure: large when an exact checker exists (Tree of Thoughts on Game of 24: 74% vs 7.3% for IO, about +66 points), small or mixed when only an LLM judge exists (ToT creative writing GPT-4 coherence 6.19 to 7.56; QDAIF human QD 0.772 vs 0.767 for a fixed few-shot prompt, which had the higher human quality rating, 4.133 vs 3.9). Cap-set and bin-packing examples need their own FunSearch citation.
agent_test: Gate search: use it only when a checker exists; otherwise single pass plus targeted check.
audit_note: Game of 24 (+66 points, ToT 74 vs IO 7.3), ToT creative-writing and QDAIF numbers match, but none of the opened sources contain cap sets or bin packing (FunSearch results not in the evidence), so those oracle examples are unsupported here.
claim_before_audit: Search benefit depends on task structure: large when an oracle exists (Game of 24 +66 points, cap sets, bin packing), small or mixed when only an LLM judge exists; a fixed few-shot prompt can match fancier quality-diversity search on human quality.

claim: On tasks with a cheap checker, many parallel tries plus the checker are a strong baseline against one long thought: NoThinking best-of-N is comparable to full thinking at up to 9x lower latency (AMC23 51.3 vs 28.9 at 700 tokens); for o1-like models correct answers are shorter than wrong ones and parallel scaling gave better coverage than sequential revision; at a 128-call budget repeated sampling beat all tree variants on ARC-AGI, but adaptive-branching tree search (AB-MCTS) beat repeated sampling on LiveCodeBench and CodeContest and on ARC with larger budgets.
agent_test: At equal tokens compare k short tries + checker vs one long chain vs tree; report success per token.
audit_note: NoThinking (51.3 vs 28.9 at 700 tokens, comparable at up to 9x latency) and Zeng (correct answers shorter, parallel coverage better) match, but Inoue shows repeated sampling beat tree variants on ARC-AGI only at the 128-call budget; AB-MCTS beat repeated sampling on LiveCodeBench and CodeContest (which have test checkers) and passed it on ARC with DeepSeek-V3 at budgets 200-512, so the general 'beat a deep tree' wording is too wide.
claim_before_audit: On tasks with a cheap checker, many parallel tries plus the checker beat one long thought or a deep tree at equal tokens: NoThinking best-of-N matches full thinking at up to 9x lower latency (AMC23 51.3 vs 28.9 at 700 tokens); for o1-like models correct answers are shorter than wrong ones and parallel scaling gave better coverage; repeated sampling beat all tree variants on ARC-AGI.

claim: No matched-compute test of tree search against best-of-N plus verifier on soft-criteria tasks (open design, planning with fuzzy goals) was found. All matched-compute studies use exact answers, unit tests or a trained reward model. The key gap-1 question is open.
agent_test: Build the test: same item set, soft rubric scored by an independent model, equal dollars and total tokens.

claim: History-aware exploration can raise accuracy, not just novelty, at a fixed budget on checkable tasks: BASIN visit penalty gave Game of 24 gpt-4o-mini 66.0 to 72.0, Qwen3-27B 43.0 to 65.0, MuSR gpt-oss-120b 63.3 to 67.0; a flat penalty hurt GPT-4 (67.0 to 61.0) until made quality-aware (70.0). Counter-evidence: sibling-scoped memory and UCT constant did nothing on MLE-bench, and Heuresis exploration gates raised diversity but not top score. One author, no replication.
agent_test: Add a tried-approach ledger with damping for strong approaches; measure final score and distinct strategies per token.

claim: Cheap diversity at fixed calls: stated-probability list prompts (Verbalized Sampling) beat direct, list and multi-turn prompts in human-rated diversity with similar quality; higher temperature buys diversity at a quality cost and mostly adds invented names on grounded tasks (CreativityBench); different models are 71-82% similar, so cross-model sampling adds little (8 distinct models among the 50 nearest answers). No ranking of ledger vs VS vs temperature at equal tokens exists, and no test on current reasoning models.
agent_test: Equal-call comparison: ledger vs VS vs persona vs temperature, scored by distinct valid solutions and by an independent check.

claim: Internal search in reasoning models is real but task dependent and token-costly: trained backtracking depth that works is 0 for ARC-1D, 1 for Countdown, 5+ for Sudoku, and QwQ-32B scores 0.0% on 4x4 Sudoku where a small model with five backtracks gets 28.9-32.1%. No study was found that adds an external ToT or MCTS scaffold to a current reasoning model at equal tokens.
agent_test: Run a reasoning model with and without an external search at equal total tokens on a hard combinatorial set.

claim: Guardrail comparison for proxy exploitation: an inline auditor agent is the cheapest first guard and caught fabrications that otherwise all reached the archive, but did not catch benchmark specialisation (13 RL runs); a held-out evaluation caught those; hiding the checker from the optimised agent lowered hacking. Execution alone did not help: fabricated run logs passed.
agent_test: Keep a held-out check the optimised steps never see; add an auditor that reads artifacts, not claims.

claim: In-prompt search (Algorithm of Thoughts) used 1 query and about 6.4k tokens against ToT's 109 queries and about 19.4k tokens on Game of 24 (GPT-4: 71% vs 69%), and about 25x fewer total tokens on crosswords. No re-test on newer models or other tasks was found.
agent_test: Re-test with a worked search trace in the prompt on a current model and a non-puzzle task.

claim: Independent replication of Creative Beam Search (31 raters, one 7B model) and of QDAIF's small human evaluation was not found in this pass; 'no replication found' is limited by search quota.
agent_test: Treat both as single-study results.
